title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & internal tools
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary: This page consolidates Redwood's core employee handbook topics: how we work, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks overview, high-level hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools new hires and managers should know. Use this as the single-source reference; operational details (team-level onboarding, interview rubrics, payroll questions) live on the linked team pages and HR portal.

Purpose & scope:
- Purpose: Provide a concise, searchable reference for new and existing employees covering expectations, career growth, benefits, and the tools required to be productive at Redwood.
- Scope: Company-wide; applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and long-term interns unless a team-specific policy overrides this document.

1) Working at Redwood — core principles
- Developer-first, production-focused: we prioritize reliability, measurable outcomes (latency, cost, accuracy), and customer impact.
- Blamelessness and learning: incidents and postmortems are oriented toward prevention and improvement.
- Asynchronous collaboration: use Confluence and Slack for documented decisions; meetings are used for alignment.
- Ownership: teams own their services, SLOs, and on-call rotations.

2) Role families & career ladders (high-level)
- Role families: Engineering (infra, runtime, platform, SRE), Product, Research/Applied ML, DevRel/Docs, People Ops, Finance, Sales/CS, Security/Compliance.
- Career ladder structure (applies to ICs and managers):
  1. IC levels: Associate / IC2 -> IC3 -> Senior (IC4) -> Staff (IC5) -> Principal (IC6)
  2. Manager levels: Manager -> Senior Manager -> Director -> Senior Director
- Expectations by tier (short):
  - IC2 (Associate): Executes tasks with guidance; learns codebase; contributes to team goals.
  - IC3 (Mid): Owns features; reliable delivery; reviews peers; participates in on-call rotation.
  - IC4 (Senior): Leads complex projects end-to-end; mentors others; shapes technical direction.
  - IC5 (Staff): Cross-team technical leader; influences architecture, performance, and cost tradeoffs.
  - Manager/Director: Sets team priorities, hires and develops talent, balances roadmap and reliability.
- Promotions: Quarterly calibration cycles. Promotion packet must include impact examples, metrics, reviewer list, and manager evaluation. See linked "promotion-guidelines" page for templates.

3) Benefits & perks (overview)
- Health: Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tier options; Redwood covers a majority of employee-only premiums.
- Financial: Competitive base, equity grants, 401(k) with employer match (US), and annual compensation review cycle.
- Time off: Flexible PTO, 12 company holidays (including winter break), parental leave (primary and secondary leave policies).
- Wellness & learning: $1,200/year L&D stipend, monthly wellness stipend, Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
- Remote & hybrid: Flexible remote-first working model with optional office days; stipends for home office equipment.
- Perks: Commuter benefits (where available), conference budget (manager approval), referral bonus program.
- How to enroll: Benefits enrollment is done in the HRIS portal during new-hire onboarding or during annual open enrollment. See "HRIS enrollment guide" for step-by-step screenshots.

4) Hiring process & new-hire onboarding (end-to-end)
- Hiring overview (phases):
  1. Requisition creation and approval (Hiring manager + People Ops partner)
  2. Sourcing & outreach (Talent Acquisition)
  3. Phone screen -> Technical assessment (as appropriate) -> Onsite loop / virtual loop -> Offer
  4. Offer acceptance -> Background check -> Preboarding
- Interview best practices: Use standardized rubrics, ensure at least one behavioral interviewer and one role-specific technical interviewer, share interviewer packet 48+ hours before loop. Panels should evaluate role-specific criteria and Redwood values (ownership, collaboration, product sense).
- Offer & comp: People Ops prepares an offer package including base, equity, target bonus (if applicable), and benefits summary. Offers are extended by the hiring manager after HR confirmation.
- New-hire checklist (first 30 days):
  - Day -3 to 0: Confirm start date, equipment request, add to Slack, issue Okta invite and access to HRIS.
  - Day 0: Welcome e-mail, manager 1:1 scheduled, team intro, mandatory security and compliance training assigned.
  - Week 1: Orientation session (company mission, product primer, key contacts), access to repos and services, small onboarding task assigned.
  - Month 1: Initial goals discussion, 30-day check-in with manager and People Ops, finalize learning plan.
- Manager responsibilities for onboarding:
  - Preboarding: Ensure equipment and accounts are provisioned; add new hire to team calendar and Slack channels.
  - First week: Pair on a small project, review team architecture and SLOs, set 30/60/90 goals.
  - Ongoing: Weekly 1:1s, performance feedback, support social integration.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)
- Identity & SSO:
  - Okta: primary SSO provider. Use your Redwood e-mail to sign in; approve device prompts for MFA. Contact security@redwood.ai for MFA exceptions.
  - Access requests: Use the Access Request form in Confluence (link: /confluence/access-requests) and follow the RBAC policy for approvals.
- Communication & docs:
  - Slack: Company-wide communication. Use channel naming conventions: #team-<name>, #proj-<name>, #ops-<service>. Keep threads on-topic and use huddles for quick syncs.
  - Confluence: Canonical docs and runbooks. Use page templates ("Team Home", "Runbook", "Postmortem") and add labels for discoverability.
- Code & reviews:
  - GitHub: Primary code host. Repos contain CONTRIBUTING.md with branching strategy; required checks: CI, security-scan, and two reviewer approvals for main merges.
  - Code review etiquette: Small PRs, descriptive titles, link to ticket, tag reviewers, respond to feedback within 48 business hours.
- Issue tracking & roadmaps:
  - Jira: sprint boards, backlog grooming, and ticket lifecycle. Use the "Component" field to indicate service ownership.
  - Product roadmap: Documented in the product workspace; high-level goals updated quarterly.
- Observability & incident response:
  - Dashboards: Grafana (latency/cost), Kibana (logs), and Datadog for traces and synthetic checks.
  - Incident channel pattern: #inc-<service> created automatically by PagerDuty integration during on-call incidents. Follow the runbook and declare severity within 30 minutes.
- HR & finance systems:
  - HRIS: ADP/BambooHR (depending on region) for payroll, PTO requests, and benefits enrollment.
  - Expense reporting: Expensify — submit receipts within 30 days and tag expenses to cost centers.

6) Security and compliance basics for all employees
- Mandatory trainings: Security awareness and data handling within first week.
- Data handling: Treat customer data as sensitive; follow the Data Residency and Retention policy for storage details.
- Secrets: Use the secrets manager (Vault) or approved KMS; never store credentials in repos.

7) Sample runbook excerpt (for reference)
- Title: Service X high CPU alert response
- Trigger: Grafana alert trigger when CPU > 85% for 5 minutes
- Steps:
  1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and create an incident channel.
  2. Check dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/123/service-x-overview.
  3. Identify recent deploys: git log --since="24 hours" --oneline && kubectl rollout status deployment/service-x.
  4. If rollout is recent, rollback using: kubectl rollout undo deployment/service-x --to-revision=<rev>.
  5. If resource saturation, scale: kubectl scale deployment/service-x --replicas=<n> or add burst capacity via Redwood Dedicated console.
  6. Postmortem: submit within 72 hours using the Postmortem template.

8) Escalations & support contacts
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (benefits, hiring, onboarding)
- IT & equipment: it-support@redwood.ai
- Security incidents: security@redwood.ai (24/7 pager)
- Payroll & finance: payroll@redwood.ai
